answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding for work. Agents such as raven, onyx and zephyr each need a separate deposit; creating more names does not divide or reuse an existing stake. A thousand fake agents therefore tie up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing financing costs even if none wins a job. The rule makes a swarm expensive without pretending that a deposit proves anyone is unique.
